g.title: Rival role demand: C — keeper demand strong (riv_fills_share ρ 0.78 on keeper lots); bowling / Indian demand effectively invisible: mkt_scarcity_bowling / _indians sit at the clip value 5 in 100% / 100% of decisions; riv_fills_share pools keeper, bowling, Indians and squad-count needs
g.text: visible for keepers, saturated / pooled for the other requirements

g.title: Rival keeper demand: B — strong (mkt_scarcity_keeper ρ -0.69; between-cell share of 'rivals needing a keeper' 0.999)
g.text: recoverable from scarcity × supply × own need

g.title: Rival keeper stockpiling: C — holdings level largely inferable: 91% (max held by one rival), 94% (rivals holding ≥ 2) and 90% (non-needing rivals able to buy) of the variance lies between cells of the observed keeper features; the WILLINGNESS of non-needing rivals to buy is not encoded anywhere (the planner, the shield and the observation count only rivals that NEED a keeper) — at the M1 forced bids that were lost, 0.34 rivals needed a keeper on average vs 5.0 non-needing rivals able to buy

g.text: own overseas state is direct; rivals' overseas capacity is not encoded
